def eliminated_teams(wins, remaining):
    """Robot battle league: which teams are already out of the running?

    There are n teams, numbered 0..n-1 (2 <= n <= 20).  Team i has won
    wins[i] matches so far (0 <= wins[i] <= 100).  remaining is an n x n
    symmetric matrix of non-negative ints with remaining[i][i] == 0 and
    0 <= remaining[i][j] <= 20: teams i and j will still play exactly
    remaining[i][j] matches against each other.  Every match is played and
    has exactly one winner (no draws); matches between other teams also
    add to those teams' win totals.

    A team k is ELIMINATED if there is NO way to decide the winners of all
    remaining matches (including k's own) such that k finishes with at
    least as many total wins as every other team (finishing tied for the
    most wins counts as NOT eliminated).

    Return the sorted (ascending) list of 0-based indices of all
    eliminated teams.  Return an empty list if no team is eliminated.

    Note: a team may be eliminated even if its maximum possible win total
    matches or exceeds every current total, because the remaining matches
    among the other teams must hand out wins to somebody.

    >>> eliminated_teams([3, 1], [[0, 1], [1, 0]])
    [1]
    >>> eliminated_teams([3, 3, 1], [[0, 2, 1], [2, 0, 1], [1, 1, 0]])
    [2]
    >>> eliminated_teams([2, 2], [[0, 2], [2, 0]])
    []
    """
